svg.title: The same J​SON text parsed by basic_json::parse() and by json_document::parse()
svg.desc: The text {"port": 6379, "price": 19.90, "tags": ["eu", "a\"b"]}. Top: basic_json::parse() builds a tree: the root json value points to a std::map whose three nodes are separate heap allocations; the price is stored as the double 19.9; the tags array is a std::vector of two json values, each pointing to its own std::string. Bottom: json_document::parse() keeps the 54 bytes of source text and builds a flat index of nine 16-byte nodes in document order: object, key port, unsigned integer 6379 (the converted value is in the node), key price, float, key tags, array, string eu, and an escaped string. Keys, the float, and the plain string point back into the source text; the escaped string points into the document's buffer of decoded strings. A json_view is two pointers: one to the document and one to a node, here the array.
svg.text: basic_json::parse(): a tree, every array, object, and string in its own heap allocation
json_document::parse(): the source text stays where it is; one flat index of 16-byte nodes
source text, 54 bytes (borrowed, or owned by the document)
json_document: owns the node index and the buffer of decoded strings
node index: 9 nodes × 16 bytes = 144 bytes, in document order
integers are converted while parsing and kept in their node;
floats and strings point back into the text
